items.question_text: Your organization has decided to move their on-premises Apache Spark-based workload to Google Cloud. You want to be able to manage the code without needing to provision and manage your own cluster. What should you do?
items.solution_text: Dataproc Serverless is specifically designed to run Apache Spark jobs without requiring users to provision or manage cluster infrastructure, aligning perfectly with the requirement to avoid managing your own cluster. In contrast, Dataproc on Compute Engine (D) requires manual cluster management, while GKE-based options (B and C) still necessitate maintaining the underlying Kubernetes control plane and nodes.

choices.text: Migrate the Spark jobs to Dataproc Serverless.
Configure a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster with Spark operators, and deploy the Spark jobs.
Migrate the Spark jobs to Dataproc on Google Kubernetes Engine.
Migrate the Spark jobs to Dataproc on Compute Engine.

items.question_text: You are developing a data ingestion pipeline to load small CSV files into BigQuery from Cloud Storage. You want to load these files upon arrival to minimize data latency. You want to accomplish this with minimal cost and maintenance. What should you do?
items.solution_text: Cloud Run functions provide an event-driven, serverless architecture that triggers immediately upon file arrival in Cloud Storage, minimizing latency while ensuring minimal cost and maintenance compared to always-on or scheduled services. Option B is the most tempting alternative but is inferior because scheduling a run every 10 minutes introduces unnecessary delay (latency) and incurs costs for infrastructure idle time between runs, violating the 'minimal' constraints.

choices.text: Use the bq command-line tool within a Cloud Shell instance to load the data into BigQuery.
Create a Cloud Composer pipeline to load new files from Cloud Storage to BigQuery and schedule it to run every 10 minutes.
Create a Cloud Run function to load the data into BigQuery that is triggered when data arrives in Cloud Storage.
Create a Dataproc cluster to pull CSV files from Cloud Storage, process them using Spark, and write the results to BigQuery.

items.question_text: Your organization has a petabyte of application logs stored as Parquet files in Cloud Storage. You need to quickly perform a one-time SQL-based analysis of the files and join them to data that already resides in BigQuery. What should you do?
items.solution_text: Option C is correct because BigQuery external tables allow you to query data directly from Cloud Storage without loading it, which is the fastest method for a one-time analysis of petabyte-scale data. Loading such a large volume (Option D) would be time-consuming and costly, while using Dataproc or Data Fusion (Options A and B) introduces unnecessary complexity and overhead for a simple SQL join task.

choices.text: Create a Dataproc cluster, and write a PySpark job to join the data from BigQuery to the files in Cloud Storage.
Launch a Cloud Data Fusion environment, use plugins to connect to BigQuery and Cloud Storage, and use the SQL join operation to analyze the data.
Create external tables over the files in Cloud Storage, and perform SQL joins to tables in BigQuery to analyze the data.
Use the bq load command to load the Parquet files into BigQuery, and perform SQL joins to analyze the data.

items.question_text: Your team is building several data pipelines that contain a collection of complex tasks and dependencies that you want to execute on a schedule, in a specific order. The tasks and dependencies consist of files in Cloud Storage, Apache Spark jobs, and data in BigQuery. You need to design a system that can schedule and automate these data processing tasks using a fully managed approach. What should you do?
items.solution_text: Cloud Composer is Google Cloud's fully managed workflow orchestration service based on Apache Airflow, specifically designed to handle complex dependencies via Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs). It provides native operators for BigQuery, Dataflow/Spark, and Cloud Storage, fulfilling the requirement for a fully managed solution without the operational overhead of self-hosting Airflow on GKE (Option D) or the limited scheduling capabilities of Cloud Scheduler/Tasks (Options A and B).

choices.text: Use Cloud Scheduler to schedule the jobs to run.
Use Cloud Tasks to schedule and run the jobs asynchronously.
Create directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) in Cloud Composer. Use the appropriate operators to connect to Cloud Storage, Spark, and BigQuery.
Create directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) in Apache Airflow deployed on Google Kubernetes Engine. Use the appropriate operators to connect to Cloud Storage, Spark, and BigQuery.
